signals.title: USD/CAD — Geopolitical Trade Shock + G10 Laggard
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3835, extending its intraday advance by 0.52% as a trade war between the US and Canada escalates following new tariff headlines. This geopolitical shock directly impacts the Canadian Dollar, which now registers as a G10 laggard with a -0.280% weekly average. The pair is currently testing its SMA200 at 1.3843, a level that has capped recent upside attempts and remains the primary technical hurdle. While the Fed 3.75% vs BoC 2.25% spread offers a +150bp carry advantage for the USD, the immediate driver is the repricing of trade-related risk. BoC holds at 2.25%. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; tariff escalation overrides positive CAD economic surprises. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep — 100% hold priced. Risk: De-escalation in trade rhetoric triggers a sharp mean-reversion toward the SMA20 at 1.3954.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: AUD/CHF presents a dominant bilateral theme as the G10 leader AUD (+0.686% avg) faces the laggard CHF (-0.389% avg), creating a 1.076% spread. The pair is supported by a massive +435bp carry premium as RBA holds at 4.35% vs SNB at 0.00%. Retail sentiment is at an extreme with 87% short AUD/CHF, diverging from the institutional trend and suggesting a contrarian risk of a further squeeze higher. Despite a negative Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of -10.3 for AUD, the carry and G10 momentum continue to favor the Australian Dollar. Technical support for AUD/USD at the SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.6954-0.7057) provides a stable base for AUD-related crosses. Trade bias: Long AUD/CHF; carry premium and bilateral momentum remain the primary drivers. Catalyst: RBA minutes next session. Risk: VIX breaks above 25, triggering a flight to safety that favors the CHF and compresses the carry trade.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Correlation Break + Options Complacency
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.16, holding just below its SMA20 at 159.43. A significant correlation break is active as USD/JPY vs VIX rises to +0.435 (z=+2.07σ), indicating that the Yen has ceased to function as a safe-haven asset in the current regime. This decoupling occurs despite a strong USDJPY 25d risk reversal at -1.96, which shows heavy institutional demand for downside protection. The OIS-based carry differential of +265bp (SOFR 3.63% vs TONA 0.98%) continues to anchor the pair's floor, even as markets settle into a calmer tone. A negative VRP of -1.6% suggests that while puts are being bought, the options market may still be underpricing the potential for realized volatility if intervention risk returns. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY; carry advantage persists while safe-haven flows remain redirected. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 66% hike priced) 18 Sep. Risk: Sudden BoJ/MoF intervention on a break above 160.00 forces a disorderly carry unwind.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Technical Support
signals.text: GBP/USD remains firm at 1.3639, supported by its SMA20/50/200 cluster between 1.3395 and 1.3485. The options market is pricing in a significant volatility risk premium (VRP) of +5.1%, with IV at 11.0% vs HV30 at 5.9%, signaling high demand for protection despite the current lack of a directional breakout. COT positioning shows a crowded long in GBP with lev_net at +46,070 (94th percentile), which typically warrants caution for late-trend exhaustion. However, the carry remains neutral (0bp) and the ESI at -8.3 suggests modest data disappointment is already priced in. Given the lack of a strong 25d RR skew (-0.06), the institutional market is currently on the sidelines regarding a directional bet. Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD; elevated vol premium suggests range-bound trading until a macro catalyst emerges. Catalyst: US PCE release. Risk: A close below the SMA200 at 1.3427 invalidates the current bullish structure.
